themes_detail.label: Door/Window Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Door and window complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1020% increase (z-score 7.44)—suggesting either weather-related damage, break-ins, or structural issues affecting multiple buildings in South Beach/Dongan Hills this week.
evidence: 7 door/window complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 7.44 indicates statistically significant anomaly
1020% spike suggests acute, localized event rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Were these complaints concentrated in one building or neighborhood block? Was there a weather event (high winds, storms) that triggered damage?
Are residents reporting break-ins or attempted break-ins as the driver of complaints?

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints jumped to 20 THIS WEEK, a 290% increase from the 8-week baseline of 5.1 per week (z-score 6.58), indicating a concentrated outbreak of sanitation, pest, or waste management problems in the district this week.
evidence: 20 unsanitary condition complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.58 indicates highly significant deviation
Spike aligns with community board's recurring 'Other expense request for DSNY' budget items, suggesting chronic sanitation understaffing
reporting_angles: Are complaints clustering in specific neighborhoods (South Beach vs. Dongan Hills) or are they district-wide?
Is this tied to missed garbage collection, rodent infestations, or accumulation of waste on streets or in buildings?

themes_detail.label: Elevator Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints surged to 5 LAST WEEK, a 900% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.5 per week (z-score 9.0), indicating widespread mechanical failures or safety issues in multi-story residential or commercial buildings across the district.
evidence: 5 elevator complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 9.0 is the highest-ranking spike in dataset
900% spike suggests simultaneous failures across multiple buildings rather than single-building issue
reporting_angles: Were elevator failures concentrated in one or two older residential buildings, or were they scattered across the district?
Are building owners delaying repairs, or are complaints reflecting a backlog of maintenance issues?

themes_detail.label: Bus Stop Shelter Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Bus stop shelter complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, a 2300% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.1 per week (z-score 8.69), suggesting either widespread shelter damage, placement problems, or a community organizing effort around transit infrastructure in South Beach/Dongan Hills.
evidence: 3 bus stop shelter complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extremely rare baseline event
Aligns with community board's recurring DOT budget requests, signaling long-standing transit advocacy
reporting_angles: Are complaints about shelter placement (accessibility, safety, weather protection) or about deteriorating physical condition?
Has a community group or block association recently mobilized around transit infrastructure needs?

themes_detail.label: Paint/Plaster Deterioration Increase
themes_detail.summary: Paint and plaster complaints rose to 8 LAST WEEK, a 300% increase from the 8-week baseline of 2.0 per week (z-score 5.37), potentially reflecting age-related building maintenance backlogs or water damage cascading from the elevated water system complaints (909 over 90 days) also affecting the district.
evidence: 8 paint/plaster complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Water system complaints (909 total over 90 days) may be root cause of interior paint/plaster damage in buildings
reporting_angles: Is paint/plaster deterioration driven by water damage from pipe leaks or moisture issues?
Are complaints concentrated in older buildings or public housing, suggesting deferred maintenance?
